# Shuffle-partition experiment

**Draft, awaiting the author's review (revision 1).** Nothing in this document is implemented,
measured or committed. The pipeline has no partition flags and records no execution plans yet, and
no run has been made. Every part may change at review. Once approved, this document becomes Part A,
together with the author's predictions (section 11). It is committed with the code changes of
section 4 before any measured run, after the prerequisites of 3.5. Part B (results and answers)
will follow section 13; the draft history stays at the end.

_Drafted with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) on 2026-10-19 from the author's decisions listed in 1.2, from
`spark_pipeline.py`, `measure.py`, `windows.py` and `tests/conftest.py`, and from the stride
experiment's records. Everything not listed in 1.2 is Claude Code's proposal; section 13 lists these
proposals by section. Revision 1, the same day, applies the findings of a read-only review of the
first draft by a separate Claude Code session (036c80c6), as the draft history lists. The author's
authorship line follows the review._

This experiment changes neither the stride experiment ([experiments.md](experiments.md)) nor its
predictions, records or collector. It writes only under `data/outputs-partitions/`.

## 1. Question and decisions

### 1.1 Question

For a fixed workload, how do the requested number of shuffle partitions and AQE's partition
coalescing change runtime and peak memory, and do they change any result? This is the partitioning
part of research question 3 (spec §2). The data, model, window set, leverages, code and all other
Spark settings stay fixed. The machine is the stride experiment's (Apple M2 MacBook Air, 8 cores,
8 GiB RAM).

### 1.2 Decided by the author (2026-10-19)

- Three configurations, A, B and C (2.1), with AQE enabled in all of them.
- The stride-7 window set of the stride experiment as the only workload (2.2).
- Order A–B–C–C–B–A, with four fresh-process runs per protocol: one warm-up, three measured (2.3).
- Code and dependency hashes are identical across all new runs, and the input checksums are
  verified. The new code hashes need not match the code that built the window set (3.1, 10).
- Settings are verified through the recorded configuration and the execution plans (6). Task
  counts are observations, not pass/fail criteria (5).
- `paired` and `path_summary` of every run are compared with A by their full keys: missing and
  duplicate keys, row counts, NULLs, breach flags, and numeric values within an explicit
  tolerance (7).
- Deferred: other configurations and extensive diagnostic tooling (12).

## 2. Configurations, workload and order

### 2.1 Configurations

| Configuration | `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` | `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled` | `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled` | Role |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 200 | `true` | `true` | Spark's default values, set explicitly (2.4); the stride experiment left them unset |
| B | 200 | `true` | `false` | the same requested count, not coalesced |
| C | 8 | `true` | `false` | one partition per core (`default_parallelism` is 8), not coalesced |

All other settings are the pipeline's (`local[*]`, UI off, UTC session time zone) and Spark's
defaults. Because AQE stays enabled, its other runtime rules still apply in B and C. For example,
it can turn a sort-merge join into a broadcast join and then read that shuffle locally. Only
coalescing is switched off.

A against B shows what coalescing does with 200 requested partitions. B against C shows what the
requested count does without coalescing. A against C compares Spark's defaults with an explicit
small count.

### 2.2 Workload

The workload is the stride-7 set in `data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7`,
unchanged: 5,364 windows and 1,351,728 window-member rows (experiments.md 2.2). Its runs in the
stride experiment wrote 2,698,866 path-day rows. It is the largest workload the stride experiment
admitted. Each run verifies seven SHA-256 values recorded in its `config.json` before Spark starts:
`windows.parquet`, the five daily-return files and `quality_report.json`. On any mismatch it exits
with code 3.

### 2.3 Order and repeats

There are six protocols, at positions 1 to 6: A, B, C, C, B, A. Each protocol is one
`etf_risk.measure` call with `--repeats 4`: four fresh-process runs, the first of them a warm-up.
`measure` summarizes the three measured runs that ended `ok`. Each configuration therefore has two
protocols, eight runs and six measured runs.

Each configuration's two positions average 3.5. If the protocols were evenly spaced in time, a
drift that changes linearly over the session would shift each configuration's mean by the same
amount, and its median approximately so. The spacing is not exactly even: the pauses are fixed, but
the protocols differ in length, so their start times are reported. A's two protocols span the
session (positions 1 and 6); C's run back to back (3 and 4). Section 9 shows why a linear drift
alone cannot produce a difference under its rule.

### 2.4 Commands and records

From the repository root, using the flags of 4.1 and 4.2 (not implemented yet):

```bash
caffeinate -i uv run --group measure python -m etf_risk.measure --repeats 4 -- \
    --windows data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7 \
    --out-root data/outputs-partitions/<A|B|C> \
    --shuffle-partitions <200|8> --coalesce <on|off> --record-plans
```

All three configurations pass all three flags, A as `--shuffle-partitions 200 --coalesce on`, so
they run the same code path and pay the same plan-capture cost. Records go to
`data/outputs-partitions/<A|B|C>/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7/`: one `protocol-<UTC time>.json`
per protocol, and one folder and one `.log` per run. Each configuration's two protocols share a
folder. Positions are not derived from start times; 3.4 assigns them. Nothing is written under
`data/outputs/` or `data/outputs-experiments/`.

### 2.5 Earlier records with A's settings

The stride experiment's stride-7 protocol `20261019T035809Z` ran this workload with A's values
(unset, so Spark's defaults) at commit `0e3c130`, without plan capture:

- median wall time 25.660 s (24.699–26.001 s);
- median peak total RSS 2.705 GiB, and 2.681–2.714 GiB over all four runs;
- in all four runs, summed stage task counts (5) of 53, 22, 81 and 100 in the phases
  `window_stats`, `model`, `summaries` and `checks`;
- in all four runs, 1, 40, 8 and 1 files written in `window_stats`, `path_days`, `path_summary` and
  `paired`.

These are earlier records under an older code state. They are used only descriptively (8.5).

## 3. Run conditions and stop rules

### 3.1 Code state

- One code state for all protocols: the same commit, `source_sha256` and `uv_lock_sha256`, and
  `git_worktree_clean: true`, in the `code` record of every protocol JSON and every `run.json`.
- The new code state is not compared with `windows_config.code`, the code that built the window set
  (`a7fb72d`). The window set itself must be unchanged (10, criterion 2).
- The following are committed before the first measured run: the code changes of section 4 and
  their tests, this document, and the author's predictions. `src/`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`
  then stay unchanged from the first protocol to the last.

### 3.2 Machine state before each protocol

The conditions of experiments.md 3.2 apply:

- Low Power Mode off and mains power;
- Docker Desktop, VS Code and other apps quit;
- a 5-minute pause;
- at least 3.0 GiB available just before the start.

Proposed additions, from the stride experiment's run log (experiments.md 5.2, 5.3):

- No protocol starts within 30 minutes of a boot (`sysctl -n kern.boottime`).
- The 5-minute load average, read just before the start, is at most a limit the author sets (4.0
  is suggested).
- After any app is quit, the checks are repeated, so the run log shows the state at the start.

Session helpers in a new file write these checks into a run log. `docs/stride-session.zsh` stays
unchanged, since experiments.md 5.2 cites it by hash.

### 3.3 Stop rules, aborts and failures

- `measure`'s stop rule is unchanged (60% of physical RAM, 4.80 GiB).
- A run that takes longer than 3× the author's predicted median for its configuration (11) is
  aborted with the abort step of the new session helpers. Like `abort_run` in
  `docs/stride-session.zsh`, it asks for confirmation, kills only the pipeline process and writes
  the abort into the run log. The commands in experiments.md 3.6 are not pasted: pasted with its
  `#` comment, that line matched about 68 unrelated processes in the author's zsh on 2026-10-18,
  because `interactivecomments` is off.
- After each protocol, the helpers check that every run wrote `plans.json` (4.2). If one did not,
  the session stops, and no further protocol runs until the cause is found.
- `checks_failed`: stop the experiment and investigate before any further protocol.
- `failed` (an aborted run included) or `memory_threshold_exceeded`: `measure` stops the protocol.
  Stop the session and keep everything; re-runs follow 3.4.
- All runs and records are kept; nothing is deleted or overwritten.

### 3.4 Positions and re-runs

- The session helpers start each protocol by its position (1–6), take its configuration from the
  order of 2.3, and write the position, configuration and start time into the run log. After the
  session, the collector holds a fixed mapping from protocol id to position, filled in from the run
  log like `ROLES` in the stride collector. It checks the mapping against each protocol's recorded
  settings and start time.
- Each position allows at most one re-run, with a written reason, after `failed` or
  `memory_threshold_exceeded`. The re-run takes place in the same session, after the 3.2 checks and
  the pause, and the sequence then continues. If the sequence cannot continue the same day, it
  restarts from position 1 in a new session; the earlier protocols are kept and reported, but not
  used.
- The used protocol at a position is the last one run there. A protocol replaced by its re-run is
  kept and reported, but not used.
- If a re-run also stops, the experiment stops.

### 3.5 Prerequisites and branch

- This draft cites sections 5 and 6 of experiments.md, the stride experiment's Part B. Part B, its
  collector and the README and spec updates are committed before this experiment's Part A.
- Proposed branch: once `feature/experiments` is merged into `main` with a merge commit, a new
  branch from `main` for this experiment's code changes and Part A.

## 4. Code changes needed before any measured run (not implemented)

### 4.1 Pipeline flags

- `--shuffle-partitions N` (an integer of at least 1) sets `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`.
- `--coalesce on|off` sets `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled`.

Both are unset by default. `build_spark` already accepts a partition count.

PySpark applies a builder's options to a session that already exists (`applyModifiableSettings` in
`pyspark/sql/session.py`), so the flags would change the settings of any session the pipeline
joins. The tests create one such session for the whole test run (`local[2]`, 4 shuffle partitions;
`tests/conftest.py:40`) and call `main()` in it. Proposed:

- Inside an existing session, the pipeline refuses both flags with exit code 2 instead of changing
  that session. A test in the shared session checks this.
- A test runs the pipeline as a separate process on the tests' synthetic window set, with and
  without the flags. Without them, `run.json` records Spark's defaults (200 and `true`); with them,
  the given values.

### 4.2 Execution plans and partition counts (`--record-plans`)

The pipeline does not record execution plans yet. Proposed: a third flag, `--record-plans`, off by
default. With it, the pipeline writes `plans.json` into the run folder after the last timed phase.
Without any of the three flags, a run's records have the same contents as before, apart from the
code state.

`plans.json` holds:

- the Spark version and `spark.sql.ui.explainMode`, the format of the stored plan text. The checks
  of section 6 read Spark's default format, `formatted`.
- For every SQL execution of this run:
  - its id;
  - the phase of its jobs: `window_stats`, `model`, `summaries` or `checks`, or `bookkeeping` for
    the row counts after the timed phases;
  - its final physical plan text;
  - for each shuffle read that AQE marks (an `AQEShuffleRead` node): the mark as Spark prints it
    (for example `coalesced`, `local` or `skewed`) and the value of its "number of partitions"
    metric.

How it is collected:

- Spark keeps the final plans and metrics in its SQL status store, which the pipeline would read
  through the JVM gateway. That is an internal interface, so its use is tied to the recorded Spark
  version (4.2.0).
- Spark's listener bus fills the store in the background. Before reading, the pipeline waits until
  the bus has processed all events, with a time limit. It then checks that every captured execution
  has finished and has a final plan (`isFinalPlan=true`).
- Only this run's executions are captured: those with an id above the highest one when the run
  started. In a fresh process that is all of them; in the tests' shared session it excludes the
  queries of earlier tests.
- The capture runs after the run's status and exit code are set, with its own error handling. A
  capture error is written to `run.json`, and the status and exit code stay unchanged. Such a run
  fails criterion 3 (10), and the check after each protocol stops the session (3.3).
- The time this takes, the wait included, is recorded as `plan_capture`. It grows with the number
  of SQL executions, which is the same in A, B and C, not with the number of tasks. `wall_s` and
  `total_in_process` include it.

Spark's event log also holds plans and metrics, but it writes one record per task, so its cost
grows with the variable under test. It stays deferred (12).

Tests, each running the pipeline in a separate process on the synthetic window set unless stated:

- with `--record-plans`, `plans.json` covers every SQL execution of the run, every plan is final,
  and the explain mode is recorded;
- with `--coalesce on` and 200 partitions, at least one shuffle read is marked `coalesced` and has
  a partition count; with `--coalesce off`, none is marked `coalesced`;
- in the shared session, only the run's own executions are captured.

These tests also check what the draft assumes about Spark 4.2.0: that the status store keeps the
final plans with the UI disabled, the plan text format, and the partition metric.

### 4.3 Collector and output comparison

A separate script, `analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py`, writes
`data/outputs-partitions/measurements.csv`. It reads only `data/outputs-partitions/`, plus the
stride-7 run of section 7, which it reads without writing. It writes one row per started run, with:

- the stride experiment's columns (experiments.md 5.6);
- the configuration, read from the recorded settings, and the position (3.4);
- `plan_capture_s`, and `wall_s` minus it;
- the observations of section 5.

It also runs the checks of sections 6, 7 and 10. `analysis/collect_measurements.py` stays
unchanged: it hard-codes the stride experiment's folder, output file, five protocols and roles, and
its authorship is split (its header). The stride CSV is neither rebuilt nor written.

## 5. Measurements

| Group | Values | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time | `wall_s`; the phases `session_start`, `window_stats_and_construction_check`, `model_and_path_days`, `summaries_and_pairing`, `checks`, `total_in_process`; `plan_capture` | `measure`; `timings_seconds` in `run.json` |
| Memory | free memory before the run; peak RSS in total and per process type; samples; processes seen; threshold crossing | `measure` |
| Configuration | recorded Spark settings and environment | `spark` and `environment` in `run.json` |
| Execution plans | Spark version and explain mode; for each SQL execution of the run: phase, final plan text, marked shuffle reads with their partition counts | `plans.json` (4.2) |
| Results | status, check violations, row counts; the `paired` and `path_summary` tables | `run.json`, `checks.json`, run folder |
| Provenance | code state, verified input checksums, window config | `run.json`, protocol JSON |
| Run conditions | the 3.2 checks, boot time, load average, pauses, memory readings, positions, deviations | run log |

Reported as observations, never as pass/fail criteria:

- Summed stage task counts per phase (`stage_task_counts`): the sum of `numTasks` over the stages
  that each job of the phase lists. A stage listed by two jobs counts twice, for example a shuffle
  stage that a later job lists as skipped. The sum need not equal the number of tasks that ran;
  whether that happens here has not been checked.
- Files written per output table, counted in each run folder.
- From the plans: the partition count of each marked shuffle read (in A, the counts after
  coalescing), the reads marked `local` or `skewed`, and the joins that ran as broadcast joins. An
  unmarked shuffle read has no partition metric. Spark then reads all of the exchange's requested
  partitions, a consequence of Spark's design that is not checked here.

Summaries use the measured runs that ended `ok` in the used protocols (3.4), as experiments.md 3.7
does. They give medians and min–max of wall time, phases and peak total RSS, per protocol and per
configuration (six runs). `wall_s` and `total_in_process` include `plan_capture`. The stride
experiment's runs had no plan capture, so comparisons with them use both values minus
`plan_capture`, with the raw values reported next to them. The memory statistic is the median of
`peak_rss_total_bytes` over the measured runs. The largest value over all runs, warm-ups included,
is reported next to it.

Not measured (12): partition sizes, shuffle bytes, spill, CPU time and GC time.

## 6. Settings verification

Each run is checked against its configuration in two ways.

1. **Recorded configuration.** The `spark` section of `run.json` shows the configuration's three
   values (2.1). Every other recorded Spark setting, and the recorded environment, are identical in
   all runs of the experiment. Any difference from the stride experiment's stride-7 runs, apart from
   the varied settings, is reported.
2. **Execution plans** (`plans.json`):
   1. The file exists, covers every SQL execution of the run, holds only final plans, and records
      Spark 4.2.0 and the explain mode `formatted`.
   2. Every plan that contains an exchange is adaptive: an `AdaptiveSparkPlan` with
      `isFinalPlan=true`.
   3. Every hash- or range-partitioning exchange uses the configuration's count:
      `hashpartitioning(…, 200)` in A and B, `hashpartitioning(…, 8)` in C. Single-partition and
      broadcast exchanges do not depend on the setting; they are only listed.
   4. In B and C, no shuffle read is marked `coalesced`, whether alone or with `skewed`.
   5. In A, the coalesced reads and their partition counts are reported. Whether and where AQE
      coalesces is an outcome, not a setting.

Items 1 and 2.1–2.4 are pass/fail criteria (10, criterion 3). Item 2.5, the partition counts and
the task counts are observations.

## 7. Output comparison with A

**Reference:** run 2 of the used protocol at position 1 (3.4), the first measured run of A. Every
other run of the used protocols is compared with it, warm-ups included (23 runs). The runs of
protocols replaced by a re-run are compared as well and reported.

Run 2 of the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol is compared too. It used A's values with the
earlier code, so it shows whether the code changes of section 4 alter these two tables beyond the
tolerance. `path_days` and `window_stats` are compared by row count only, from `run.json`, for every
run. Tables are read with PyArrow, which keeps null and NaN distinct.

| Table | Full key | Rows at stride 7 |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `paired` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date` | 5,364 |
| `path_summary` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date`, `leverage` | 10,728 |

For each table, a run passes if all of these hold:

1. **Rows:** its row count equals the reference's.
2. **Keys:** no key column is null and no key occurs twice. The run and the reference have exactly
   the same keys, matched exactly, `leverage` included: none missing, none extra.
3. **Columns:** the same columns, with the same types.
4. **NULLs:** every column is null in exactly the same rows as in the reference, with rows matched
   by key.
5. **Breach fields** are equal exactly:
   - in `paired`: `breached_1x`, `breached_2x`, `breach_date_2x`, `breach_day_2x`, `last_ok_date_2x`
     and `days_ok_2x`;
   - in `path_summary`: `breached`, `n_breach_rows`, `breach_day`, `breach_date`, `last_ok_date` and
     `days_ok`.
6. **Other non-floating columns:** every other string, date, integer and boolean column is equal
   exactly.
7. **Floating-point columns other than the keys:** each value x satisfies
   `|x − r| ≤ 1e-12 + 1e-9 × |r|`, where r is the reference value, and NaN matches only NaN. The
   largest absolute and relative difference per column is reported, even when the run passes.

The tolerance is the pipeline's own tolerance for the 1x identity (`RTOL` = 1e-9, `ATOL` = 1e-12).
Spark may add the terms of a sum or average in an order that depends on partitioning, which can
change the last bits. The reported differences show how far below the tolerance they stay.

## 8. Drift rules

1. **Session drift.** If A's protocol medians at positions 1 and 6 differ by more than 10% of the
   first, drift is reported and comparisons are marked as affected. Nothing is re-run silently.
   This is the rule of experiments.md 3.4.
2. **Pairs.** The same rule applies to B (positions 2 and 5) and C (3 and 4). The C pair runs back
   to back, so it shows the variation between protocols with little time for drift.
3. **Memory.** Pairs whose median peak total RSS differs by more than 0.2 GiB are reported.
4. **Context.** For each protocol, the start time, the free memory before each run, the load
   average and the time since boot are shown next to the pair differences. No rule applies to them.
5. **Earlier records.** A is compared with the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol (2.5)
   descriptively only, with `wall_s` minus `plan_capture` (5), since the code state and the day
   differ.

Drift does not void the results. It is reported, and section 9 still applies.

## 9. Comparing configurations

For two configurations X and Y:

- d1 is the difference between their protocol medians in positions 1–3;
- d2 is the same difference in positions 4–6;
- d is the difference between the medians of their six measured runs.

Under a drift that changes linearly with position, d1 and d2 shift in opposite directions for every
pair: by one position step for A–B and for B–C, by two for A–C. A drift alone therefore gives d1
and d2 opposite signs, and the rules below never report it as a difference.

The rules:

- **Wall time.** X and Y differ if |d| is more than 10% of A's six-run median and d1, d2 and d have
  the same sign. Otherwise there is no clear difference.
- **Peak memory.** The same rule, with a threshold of 0.2 GiB on the median peak total RSS. That is
  just above the largest spread among the measured runs of one protocol in the stride experiment
  (0.185 GiB), the runs this statistic uses. Counting warm-ups, two protocols spread more (0.246
  and 0.223 GiB).
- **Phases** are described with d1, d2 and d, without a threshold.
- **Plans, partition counts, task counts and file counts** are described, not tested.

With two protocols per configuration, this is a descriptive rule, not a statistical test.

## 10. Acceptance criteria

The results are used only if all of these hold:

1. **Code state:** 3.1 holds in every protocol JSON and every `run.json` of the experiment.
2. **Inputs:** each run's `verified_sha256` holds exactly the seven inputs of 2.2, each equal to the
   hash in the stride-7 `config.json`, and each run's `windows_config` equals that file. After the
   session, the seven hashes are computed once more and are unchanged.
3. **Settings:** section 6, items 1 and 2.1–2.4, hold for every run of the used protocols.
4. **Results:** every run of the used protocols ended `ok` with zero check violations. Section 7
   passes for every run of the used protocols and for the stride-experiment run.
5. **Completeness:** each of the six positions has a used protocol (3.4) that started 4 of 4 runs,
   all of which ended `ok`. None stopped early, none was aborted, and no sample exceeded 4.80 GiB.

If criterion 1, 2 or 3 fails, no configurations are compared until the cause is found. Stops and
re-runs follow 3.3 and 3.4. Drift (section 8) is not an acceptance criterion.

Run conditions are not an acceptance criterion either. A departure from 3.2 is recorded as a
deviation, and the protocol's results are labeled with it, as in experiments.md 5.3.

## 11. Predictions

_The author writes this section before any measured run._ For each configuration it gives:

- the median wall time, with a band;
- the peak memory statistic of section 5, with a range;
- the plans, partition counts and task counts expected.

The abort limits follow from the predicted medians (3.3). The stride experiment's predictions
(experiments.md section 4) stay unchanged.

## 12. Deferred

- other partition counts, for example 2 or 32;
- running with AQE disabled;
- Spark's event log, and task counts per stage or de-duplicated by stage;
- partition sizes, shuffle bytes, spill, CPU time and GC time;
- a full comparison of `path_days`;
- caching.

## 13. Proposals awaiting review

Everything below is Claude Code's proposal; the author's decisions are in 1.2.

- **2.3–2.4:** the drift reasoning; explicit flags in all three configurations; one output folder
  per configuration.
- **3.2:** the boot wait, the load-average limit and the repeated checks.
- **3.3:** the abort step in the new helpers, the `plans.json` check after each protocol, and the
  handling of each status.
- **3.4:** positions from the run log; one re-run per position in the same session, otherwise a
  restart from position 1; which protocol is used.
- **3.5:** the branch.
- **4.1:** the flag names; refusing the flags inside an existing session; the flag tests in a
  separate process.
- **4.2:**
  - `--record-plans` and the contents of `plans.json`, including the partition counts;
  - reading Spark's SQL status store, with the wait, the scope and the error handling;
  - the tests.

  Capturing the partition counts keeps the spec's statement that requested and actual partition
  counts are recorded (spec §4 and §8, expectation 5). Without it, the spec needs rewording.
- **4.3:** a separate collector; the stride collector left unchanged.
- **5:** the summary statistics, the observations, and how runs are compared with the stride runs.
- **6:** the plan checks, and which of them are pass/fail.
- **7:** the reference run, the exact and tolerance rules with their values, and the comparison with
  the stride experiment's stride-7 run.
- **8–9:** the drift and memory thresholds and the comparison rule.
- **10:** the set of acceptance criteria, and run conditions as labels instead of a criterion.
- **12:** the contents of the deferred list.
- Part B in this file.

## Draft history

separate Claude Code session (036c80c6). Numbers are the review's.

| Finding | Change | Where |

## 1. Question and decisions

### 1.1 Question

For a fixed workload, how do the requested number of shuffle partitions and AQE's partition
coalescing change runtime and peak memory, and do they change any result? This is the partitioning
part of research question 3 (spec §2). The data, model, window set, leverages, code and all other
Spark settings stay fixed. The machine is the stride experiment's (Apple M2 MacBook Air, 8 cores,
8 GiB RAM).

### 1.2 Decided by the author (2026-10-19)

- Three configurations, A, B and C (2.1), with AQE enabled in all of them.
- The stride-7 window set of the stride experiment as the only workload (2.2).
- Order A–B–C–C–B–A, with four fresh-process runs per protocol: one warm-up, three measured (2.3).
- Code and dependency hashes are identical across all new runs, and the input checksums are
  verified. The new code hashes need not match the code that built the window set (3.1, 10).
- Settings are verified through the recorded configuration and the execution plans (6). Task

- Deferred: other configurations and extensive diagnostic tooling (12).

| Configuration | `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` | `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled` | `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled` | Role |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 200 | `true` | `true` | Spark's default values, set explicitly (2.4); the stride experiment left them unset |
| B | 200 | `true` | `false` | the same requested count, not coalesced |
| C | 8 | `true` | `false` | one partition per core (`default_parallelism` is 8), not coalesced |

All other settings are the pipeline's (`local[*]`, UI off, UTC session time zone) and Spark's
defaults. Because AQE stays enabled, its other runtime rules still apply in B and C. For example,
it can turn a sort-merge join into a broadcast join and then read that shuffle locally. Only
coalescing is switched off.

A against B shows what coalescing does with 200 requested partitions. B against C shows what the
requested count does without coalescing. A against C compares Spark's defaults with an explicit
small count.

### 2.2 Workload

The workload is the stride-7 set in `data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7`,

protocols, eight runs and six measured runs.

drift that changes linearly over the session would shift each configuration's mean by the same
amount, and its median approximately so. The spacing is not exactly even: the pauses are fixed, but
the protocols differ in length, so their start times are reported. A's two protocols span the
session (positions 1 and 6); C's run back to back (3 and 4). Section 9 shows why a linear drift
alone cannot produce a difference under its rule.

The stride experiment's stride-7 protocol `20261019T035809Z` ran this workload with A's values
(unset, so Spark's defaults) at commit `0e3c130`, without plan capture:

- median wall time 25.660 s (24.699–26.001 s);

### 3.2 Machine state before each protocol

The conditions of experiments.md 3.2 apply:

- Low Power Mode off and mains power;
- Docker Desktop, VS Code and other apps quit;
- a 5-minute pause;
- at least 3.0 GiB available just before the start.

- No protocol starts within 30 minutes of a boot (`sysctl -n kern.boottime`).
- The 5-minute load average, read just before the start, is at most a limit the author sets (4.0

unchanged, since experiments.md 5.2 cites it by hash.

- `measure`'s stop rule is unchanged (60% of physical RAM, 4.80 GiB).

- All runs and records are kept; nothing is deleted or overwritten.

### 3.4 Positions and re-runs

### 4.1 Pipeline flags

- `--shuffle-partitions N` (an integer of at least 1) sets `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`.
- `--coalesce on|off` sets `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled`.

Both are unset by default. `build_spark` already accepts a partition count.

PySpark applies a builder's options to a session that already exists (`applyModifiableSettings` in
`pyspark/sql/session.py`), so the flags would change the settings of any session the pipeline
joins. The tests create one such session for the whole test run (`local[2]`, 4 shuffle partitions;
`tests/conftest.py:40`) and call `main()` in it. Proposed:

- Inside an existing session, the pipeline refuses both flags with exit code 2 instead of changing
  that session. A test in the shared session checks this.
- A test runs the pipeline as a separate process on the tests' synthetic window set, with and
  without the flags. Without them, `run.json` records Spark's defaults (200 and `true`); with them,
  the given values.

### 4.2 Execution plans and partition counts (`--record-plans`)

The pipeline does not record execution plans yet. Proposed: a third flag, `--record-plans`, off by
default. With it, the pipeline writes `plans.json` into the run folder after the last timed phase.
Without any of the three flags, a run's records have the same contents as before, apart from the
code state.

`plans.json` holds:

- the Spark version and `spark.sql.ui.explainMode`, the format of the stored plan text. The checks
  of section 6 read Spark's default format, `formatted`.
- For every SQL execution of this run:
  - its id;
  - the phase of its jobs: `window_stats`, `model`, `summaries` or `checks`, or `bookkeeping` for
    the row counts after the timed phases;
  - its final physical plan text;
  - for each shuffle read that AQE marks (an `AQEShuffleRead` node): the mark as Spark prints it
    (for example `coalesced`, `local` or `skewed`) and the value of its "number of partitions"
    metric.

How it is collected:

- Spark keeps the final plans and metrics in its SQL status store, which the pipeline would read
  through the JVM gateway. That is an internal interface, so its use is tied to the recorded Spark
  version (4.2.0).
- Spark's listener bus fills the store in the background. Before reading, the pipeline waits until
  the bus has processed all events, with a time limit. It then checks that every captured execution
  has finished and has a final plan (`isFinalPlan=true`).
- Only this run's executions are captured: those with an id above the highest one when the run
  started. In a fresh process that is all of them; in the tests' shared session it excludes the
  queries of earlier tests.
- The capture runs after the run's status and exit code are set, with its own error handling. A
  capture error is written to `run.json`, and the status and exit code stay unchanged. Such a run
  fails criterion 3 (10), and the check after each protocol stops the session (3.3).
- The time this takes, the wait included, is recorded as `plan_capture`. It grows with the number
  of SQL executions, which is the same in A, B and C, not with the number of tasks. `wall_s` and
  `total_in_process` include it.

Spark's event log also holds plans and metrics, but it writes one record per task, so its cost
grows with the variable under test. It stays deferred (12).

Tests, each running the pipeline in a separate process on the synthetic window set unless stated:

- with `--record-plans`, `plans.json` covers every SQL execution of the run, every plan is final,
  and the explain mode is recorded;
- with `--coalesce on` and 200 partitions, at least one shuffle read is marked `coalesced` and has
  a partition count; with `--coalesce off`, none is marked `coalesced`;
- in the shared session, only the run's own executions are captured.

These tests also check what the draft assumes about Spark 4.2.0: that the status store keeps the
final plans with the UI disabled, the plan text format, and the partition metric.

### 4.3 Collector and output comparison

A separate script, `analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py`, writes
`data/outputs-partitions/measurements.csv`. It reads only `data/outputs-partitions/`, plus the
stride-7 run of section 7, which it reads without writing. It writes one row per started run, with:

- the stride experiment's columns (experiments.md 5.6);
- the configuration, read from the recorded settings, and the position (3.4);
- `plan_capture_s`, and `wall_s` minus it;
- the observations of section 5.

It also runs the checks of sections 6, 7 and 10. `analysis/collect_measurements.py` stays
unchanged: it hard-codes the stride experiment's folder, output file, five protocols and roles, and
its authorship is split (its header). The stride CSV is neither rebuilt nor written.

## 5. Measurements

| Group | Values | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time | `wall_s`; the phases `session_start`, `window_stats_and_construction_check`, `model_and_path_days`, `summaries_and_pairing`, `checks`, `total_in_process`; `plan_capture` | `measure`; `timings_seconds` in `run.json` |

Each run is checked against its configuration in two ways.

1. **Recorded configuration.** The `spark` section of `run.json` shows the configuration's three
   values (2.1). Every other recorded Spark setting, and the recorded environment, are identical in
   all runs of the experiment. Any difference from the stride experiment's stride-7 runs, apart from

2. **Execution plans** (`plans.json`):
   1. The file exists, covers every SQL execution of the run, holds only final plans, and records
      Spark 4.2.0 and the explain mode `formatted`.
   2. Every plan that contains an exchange is adaptive: an `AdaptiveSparkPlan` with
      `isFinalPlan=true`.

      `hashpartitioning(…, 200)` in A and B, `hashpartitioning(…, 8)` in C. Single-partition and
      broadcast exchanges do not depend on the setting; they are only listed.

      coalesces is an outcome, not a setting.

Items 1 and 2.1–2.4 are pass/fail criteria (10, criterion 3). Item 2.5, the partition counts and
the task counts are observations.

## 7. Output comparison with A

**Reference:** run 2 of the used protocol at position 1 (3.4), the first measured run of A. Every
other run of the used protocols is compared with it, warm-ups included (23 runs). The runs of
protocols replaced by a re-run are compared as well and reported.

Run 2 of the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol is compared too. It used A's values with the
earlier code, so it shows whether the code changes of section 4 alter these two tables beyond the
tolerance. `path_days` and `window_stats` are compared by row count only, from `run.json`, for every
run. Tables are read with PyArrow, which keeps null and NaN distinct.

| Table | Full key | Rows at stride 7 |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `paired` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date` | 5,364 |
| `path_summary` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date`, `leverage` | 10,728 |

For each table, a run passes if all of these hold:

1. **Rows:** its row count equals the reference's.
2. **Keys:** no key column is null and no key occurs twice. The run and the reference have exactly
   the same keys, matched exactly, `leverage` included: none missing, none extra.
3. **Columns:** the same columns, with the same types.
4. **NULLs:** every column is null in exactly the same rows as in the reference, with rows matched
   by key.
5. **Breach fields** are equal exactly:
   - in `paired`: `breached_1x`, `breached_2x`, `breach_date_2x`, `breach_day_2x`, `last_ok_date_2x`

6. **Other non-floating columns:** every other string, date, integer and boolean column is equal
   exactly.
7. **Floating-point columns other than the keys:** each value x satisfies

   largest absolute and relative difference per column is reported, even when the run passes.

The tolerance is the pipeline's own tolerance for the 1x identity (`RTOL` = 1e-9, `ATOL` = 1e-12).
Spark may add the terms of a sum or average in an order that depends on partitioning, which can
change the last bits. The reported differences show how far below the tolerance they stay.

## 8. Drift rules

1. **Session drift.** If A's protocol medians at positions 1 and 6 differ by more than 10% of the
   first, drift is reported and comparisons are marked as affected. Nothing is re-run silently.
   This is the rule of experiments.md 3.4.
2. **Pairs.** The same rule applies to B (positions 2 and 5) and C (3 and 4). The C pair runs back
   to back, so it shows the variation between protocols with little time for drift.
3. **Memory.** Pairs whose median peak total RSS differs by more than 0.2 GiB are reported.
4. **Context.** For each protocol, the start time, the free memory before each run, the load
   average and the time since boot are shown next to the pair differences. No rule applies to them.
5. **Earlier records.** A is compared with the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol (2.5)
   descriptively only, with `wall_s` minus `plan_capture` (5), since the code state and the day
   differ.

Drift does not void the results. It is reported, and section 9 still applies.

## 9. Comparing configurations

For two configurations X and Y:

- d1 is the difference between their protocol medians in positions 1–3;
- d2 is the same difference in positions 4–6;
- d is the difference between the medians of their six measured runs.

Under a drift that changes linearly with position, d1 and d2 shift in opposite directions for every
pair: by one position step for A–B and for B–C, by two for A–C. A drift alone therefore gives d1
and d2 opposite signs, and the rules below never report it as a difference.

The rules:

- **Wall time.** X and Y differ if |d| is more than 10% of A's six-run median and d1, d2 and d have
  the same sign. Otherwise there is no clear difference.
- **Peak memory.** The same rule, with a threshold of 0.2 GiB on the median peak total RSS. That is
  just above the largest spread among the measured runs of one protocol in the stride experiment
  (0.185 GiB), the runs this statistic uses. Counting warm-ups, two protocols spread more (0.246
  and 0.223 GiB).
- **Phases** are described with d1, d2 and d, without a threshold.
- **Plans, partition counts, task counts and file counts** are described, not tested.

With two protocols per configuration, this is a descriptive rule, not a statistical test.

## 10. Acceptance criteria

The results are used only if all of these hold:

1. **Code state:** 3.1 holds in every protocol JSON and every `run.json` of the experiment.
2. **Inputs:** each run's `verified_sha256` holds exactly the seven inputs of 2.2, each equal to the
   hash in the stride-7 `config.json`, and each run's `windows_config` equals that file. After the
   session, the seven hashes are computed once more and are unchanged.
3. **Settings:** section 6, items 1 and 2.1–2.4, hold for every run of the used protocols.
4. **Results:** every run of the used protocols ended `ok` with zero check violations. Section 7
   passes for every run of the used protocols and for the stride-experiment run.
5. **Completeness:** each of the six positions has a used protocol (3.4) that started 4 of 4 runs,
   all of which ended `ok`. None stopped early, none was aborted, and no sample exceeded 4.80 GiB.

If criterion 1, 2 or 3 fails, no configurations are compared until the cause is found. Stops and
re-runs follow 3.3 and 3.4. Drift (section 8) is not an acceptance criterion.

Run conditions are not an acceptance criterion either. A departure from 3.2 is recorded as a
deviation, and the protocol's results are labeled with it, as in experiments.md 5.3.

## 11. Predictions

_The author writes this section before any measured run._ For each configuration it gives:

- the median wall time, with a band;
- the peak memory statistic of section 5, with a range;
- the plans, partition counts and task counts expected.

(experiments.md section 4) stay unchanged.

## 1. Question and decisions

### 1.1 Question

For a fixed workload, how do the requested number of shuffle partitions and AQE's partition
coalescing change runtime and peak memory, and do they change any result? This is the partitioning
part of research question 3 (spec §2). The data, model, window set, leverages, code and all other

8 GiB RAM).

- Three configurations, A, B and C (2.1), with AQE enabled in all of them.
- The stride-7 window set of the stride experiment as the only workload (2.2).

| Configuration | `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` | `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled` | `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled` | Role |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 200 | `true` | `true` | Spark's default values, set explicitly (2.4); the stride experiment left them unset |
| B | 200 | `true` | `false` | the same requested count, not coalesced |
| C | 8 | `true` | `false` | one partition per core (`default_parallelism` is 8), not coalesced |

All other settings are the pipeline's (`local[*]`, UI off, UTC session time zone) and Spark's
defaults. Because AQE stays enabled, its other runtime rules still apply in B and C. For example,
it can turn a sort-merge join into a broadcast join and then read that shuffle locally. Only
coalescing is switched off.

A against B shows what coalescing does with 200 requested partitions. B against C shows what the
requested count does without coalescing. A against C compares Spark's defaults with an explicit
small count.

### 2.2 Workload

The workload is the stride-7 set in `data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7`,

admitted. Each run verifies seven SHA-256 values recorded in its `config.json` before Spark starts:

with code 3.

### 2.3 Order and repeats

There are six protocols, at positions 1 to 6: A, B, C, C, B, A. Each protocol is one
`etf_risk.measure` call with `--repeats 4`: four fresh-process runs, the first of them a warm-up.
`measure` summarizes the three measured runs that ended `ok`. Each configuration therefore has two
protocols, eight runs and six measured runs.

Each configuration's two positions average 3.5. If the protocols were evenly spaced in time, a
drift that changes linearly over the session would shift each configuration's mean by the same
amount, and its median approximately so. The spacing is not exactly even: the pauses are fixed, but
the protocols differ in length, so their start times are reported. A's two protocols span the
session (positions 1 and 6); C's run back to back (3 and 4). Section 9 shows why a linear drift
alone cannot produce a difference under its rule.

From the repository root, using the flags of 4.1 and 4.2 (not implemented yet):

```bash
caffeinate -i uv run --group measure python -m etf_risk.measure --repeats 4 -- \
    --windows data/windows-experiments/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7 \
    --out-root data/outputs-partitions/<A|B|C> \
    --shuffle-partitions <200|8> --coalesce <on|off> --record-plans

All three configurations pass all three flags, A as `--shuffle-partitions 200 --coalesce on`, so
they run the same code path and pay the same plan-capture cost. Records go to
`data/outputs-partitions/<A|B|C>/full-2026-10-12/rolling-252-s7/`: one `protocol-<UTC time>.json`
per protocol, and one folder and one `.log` per run. Each configuration's two protocols share a
folder. Positions are not derived from start times; 3.4 assigns them. Nothing is written under
`data/outputs/` or `data/outputs-experiments/`.

### 2.5 Earlier records with A's settings

The stride experiment's stride-7 protocol `20261019T035809Z` ran this workload with A's values
(unset, so Spark's defaults) at commit `0e3c130`, without plan capture:

- median wall time 25.660 s (24.699–26.001 s);
- median peak total RSS 2.705 GiB, and 2.681–2.714 GiB over all four runs;
- in all four runs, summed stage task counts (5) of 53, 22, 81 and 100 in the phases

- in all four runs, 1, 40, 8 and 1 files written in `window_stats`, `path_days`, `path_summary` and

These are earlier records under an older code state. They are used only descriptively (8.5).

### 3.1 Code state

- One code state for all protocols: the same commit, `source_sha256` and `uv_lock_sha256`, and

- The new code state is not compared with `windows_config.code`, the code that built the window set

- The following are committed before the first measured run: the code changes of section 4 and
  their tests, this document, and the author's predictions. `src/`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`
  then stay unchanged from the first protocol to the last.

### 3.2 Machine state before each protocol

The conditions of experiments.md 3.2 apply:

- Low Power Mode off and mains power;
- Docker Desktop, VS Code and other apps quit;
- a 5-minute pause;
- at least 3.0 GiB available just before the start.

Proposed additions, from the stride experiment's run log (experiments.md 5.2, 5.3):

- No protocol starts within 30 minutes of a boot (`sysctl -n kern.boottime`).
- The 5-minute load average, read just before the start, is at most a limit the author sets (4.0
  is suggested).
- After any app is quit, the checks are repeated, so the run log shows the state at the start.

Session helpers in a new file write these checks into a run log. `docs/stride-session.zsh` stays
unchanged, since experiments.md 5.2 cites it by hash.

### 3.3 Stop rules, aborts and failures

- `measure`'s stop rule is unchanged (60% of physical RAM, 4.80 GiB).
- A run that takes longer than 3× the author's predicted median for its configuration (11) is
  aborted with the abort step of the new session helpers. Like `abort_run` in
  `docs/stride-session.zsh`, it asks for confirmation, kills only the pipeline process and writes
  the abort into the run log. The commands in experiments.md 3.6 are not pasted: pasted with its

- `failed` (an aborted run included) or `memory_threshold_exceeded`: `measure` stops the protocol.
  Stop the session and keep everything; re-runs follow 3.4.
- All runs and records are kept; nothing is deleted or overwritten.

### 3.4 Positions and re-runs

### 3.5 Prerequisites and branch

### 4.1 Pipeline flags

- `--shuffle-partitions N` (an integer of at least 1) sets `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`.
- `--coalesce on|off` sets `spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled`.

Both are unset by default. `build_spark` already accepts a partition count.

PySpark applies a builder's options to a session that already exists (`applyModifiableSettings` in
`pyspark/sql/session.py`), so the flags would change the settings of any session the pipeline
joins. The tests create one such session for the whole test run (`local[2]`, 4 shuffle partitions;
`tests/conftest.py:40`) and call `main()` in it. Proposed:

- Inside an existing session, the pipeline refuses both flags with exit code 2 instead of changing
  that session. A test in the shared session checks this.
- A test runs the pipeline as a separate process on the tests' synthetic window set, with and
  without the flags. Without them, `run.json` records Spark's defaults (200 and `true`); with them,
  the given values.

### 4.2 Execution plans and partition counts (`--record-plans`)

The pipeline does not record execution plans yet. Proposed: a third flag, `--record-plans`, off by
default. With it, the pipeline writes `plans.json` into the run folder after the last timed phase.
Without any of the three flags, a run's records have the same contents as before, apart from the
code state.

`plans.json` holds:

- the Spark version and `spark.sql.ui.explainMode`, the format of the stored plan text. The checks
  of section 6 read Spark's default format, `formatted`.
- For every SQL execution of this run:
  - its id;
  - the phase of its jobs: `window_stats`, `model`, `summaries` or `checks`, or `bookkeeping` for
    the row counts after the timed phases;
  - its final physical plan text;
  - for each shuffle read that AQE marks (an `AQEShuffleRead` node): the mark as Spark prints it
    (for example `coalesced`, `local` or `skewed`) and the value of its "number of partitions"
    metric.

How it is collected:

- Spark keeps the final plans and metrics in its SQL status store, which the pipeline would read
  through the JVM gateway. That is an internal interface, so its use is tied to the recorded Spark
  version (4.2.0).
- Spark's listener bus fills the store in the background. Before reading, the pipeline waits until
  the bus has processed all events, with a time limit. It then checks that every captured execution
  has finished and has a final plan (`isFinalPlan=true`).
- Only this run's executions are captured: those with an id above the highest one when the run
  started. In a fresh process that is all of them; in the tests' shared session it excludes the
  queries of earlier tests.
- The capture runs after the run's status and exit code are set, with its own error handling. A
  capture error is written to `run.json`, and the status and exit code stay unchanged. Such a run
  fails criterion 3 (10), and the check after each protocol stops the session (3.3).
- The time this takes, the wait included, is recorded as `plan_capture`. It grows with the number
  of SQL executions, which is the same in A, B and C, not with the number of tasks. `wall_s` and
  `total_in_process` include it.

Spark's event log also holds plans and metrics, but it writes one record per task, so its cost
grows with the variable under test. It stays deferred (12).

Tests, each running the pipeline in a separate process on the synthetic window set unless stated:

- with `--record-plans`, `plans.json` covers every SQL execution of the run, every plan is final,
  and the explain mode is recorded;
- with `--coalesce on` and 200 partitions, at least one shuffle read is marked `coalesced` and has
  a partition count; with `--coalesce off`, none is marked `coalesced`;
- in the shared session, only the run's own executions are captured.

These tests also check what the draft assumes about Spark 4.2.0: that the status store keeps the
final plans with the UI disabled, the plan text format, and the partition metric.

### 4.3 Collector and output comparison

A separate script, `analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py`, writes
`data/outputs-partitions/measurements.csv`. It reads only `data/outputs-partitions/`, plus the
stride-7 run of section 7, which it reads without writing. It writes one row per started run, with:

- the stride experiment's columns (experiments.md 5.6);
- the configuration, read from the recorded settings, and the position (3.4);
- `plan_capture_s`, and `wall_s` minus it;
- the observations of section 5.

It also runs the checks of sections 6, 7 and 10. `analysis/collect_measurements.py` stays
unchanged: it hard-codes the stride experiment's folder, output file, five protocols and roles, and
its authorship is split (its header). The stride CSV is neither rebuilt nor written.

## 5. Measurements

| Group | Values | From |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Time | `wall_s`; the phases `session_start`, `window_stats_and_construction_check`, `model_and_path_days`, `summaries_and_pairing`, `checks`, `total_in_process`; `plan_capture` | `measure`; `timings_seconds` in `run.json` |
| Memory | free memory before the run; peak RSS in total and per process type; samples; processes seen; threshold crossing | `measure` |
| Configuration | recorded Spark settings and environment | `spark` and `environment` in `run.json` |
| Execution plans | Spark version and explain mode; for each SQL execution of the run: phase, final plan text, marked shuffle reads with their partition counts | `plans.json` (4.2) |
| Results | status, check violations, row counts; the `paired` and `path_summary` tables | `run.json`, `checks.json`, run folder |
| Provenance | code state, verified input checksums, window config | `run.json`, protocol JSON |
| Run conditions | the 3.2 checks, boot time, load average, pauses, memory readings, positions, deviations | run log |

Reported as observations, never as pass/fail criteria:

- Summed stage task counts per phase (`stage_task_counts`): the sum of `numTasks` over the stages
  that each job of the phase lists. A stage listed by two jobs counts twice, for example a shuffle
  stage that a later job lists as skipped. The sum need not equal the number of tasks that ran;
  whether that happens here has not been checked.
- Files written per output table, counted in each run folder.
- From the plans: the partition count of each marked shuffle read (in A, the counts after
  coalescing), the reads marked `local` or `skewed`, and the joins that ran as broadcast joins. An
  unmarked shuffle read has no partition metric. Spark then reads all of the exchange's requested
  partitions, a consequence of Spark's design that is not checked here.

Summaries use the measured runs that ended `ok` in the used protocols (3.4), as experiments.md 3.7
does. They give medians and min–max of wall time, phases and peak total RSS, per protocol and per
configuration (six runs). `wall_s` and `total_in_process` include `plan_capture`. The stride
experiment's runs had no plan capture, so comparisons with them use both values minus
`plan_capture`, with the raw values reported next to them. The memory statistic is the median of
`peak_rss_total_bytes` over the measured runs. The largest value over all runs, warm-ups included,
is reported next to it.

Not measured (12): partition sizes, shuffle bytes, spill, CPU time and GC time.

## 6. Settings verification

Each run is checked against its configuration in two ways.

1. **Recorded configuration.** The `spark` section of `run.json` shows the configuration's three
   values (2.1). Every other recorded Spark setting, and the recorded environment, are identical in
   all runs of the experiment. Any difference from the stride experiment's stride-7 runs, apart from
   the varied settings, is reported.
2. **Execution plans** (`plans.json`):
   1. The file exists, covers every SQL execution of the run, holds only final plans, and records
      Spark 4.2.0 and the explain mode `formatted`.
   2. Every plan that contains an exchange is adaptive: an `AdaptiveSparkPlan` with
      `isFinalPlan=true`.
   3. Every hash- or range-partitioning exchange uses the configuration's count:
      `hashpartitioning(…, 200)` in A and B, `hashpartitioning(…, 8)` in C. Single-partition and
      broadcast exchanges do not depend on the setting; they are only listed.
   4. In B and C, no shuffle read is marked `coalesced`, whether alone or with `skewed`.
   5. In A, the coalesced reads and their partition counts are reported. Whether and where AQE
      coalesces is an outcome, not a setting.

Items 1 and 2.1–2.4 are pass/fail criteria (10, criterion 3). Item 2.5, the partition counts and
the task counts are observations.

## 7. Output comparison with A

**Reference:** run 2 of the used protocol at position 1 (3.4), the first measured run of A. Every
other run of the used protocols is compared with it, warm-ups included (23 runs). The runs of
protocols replaced by a re-run are compared as well and reported.

Run 2 of the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol is compared too. It used A's values with the
earlier code, so it shows whether the code changes of section 4 alter these two tables beyond the
tolerance. `path_days` and `window_stats` are compared by row count only, from `run.json`, for every
run. Tables are read with PyArrow, which keeps null and NaN distinct.

| Table | Full key | Rows at stride 7 |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `paired` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date` | 5,364 |
| `path_summary` | `window_kind`, `ticker`, `window_days`, `entry_date`, `leverage` | 10,728 |

For each table, a run passes if all of these hold:

1. **Rows:** its row count equals the reference's.
2. **Keys:** no key column is null and no key occurs twice. The run and the reference have exactly
   the same keys, matched exactly, `leverage` included: none missing, none extra.
3. **Columns:** the same columns, with the same types.
4. **NULLs:** every column is null in exactly the same rows as in the reference, with rows matched
   by key.
5. **Breach fields** are equal exactly:
   - in `paired`: `breached_1x`, `breached_2x`, `breach_date_2x`, `breach_day_2x`, `last_ok_date_2x`
     and `days_ok_2x`;
   - in `path_summary`: `breached`, `n_breach_rows`, `breach_day`, `breach_date`, `last_ok_date` and
     `days_ok`.
6. **Other non-floating columns:** every other string, date, integer and boolean column is equal
   exactly.
7. **Floating-point columns other than the keys:** each value x satisfies
   `|x − r| ≤ 1e-12 + 1e-9 × |r|`, where r is the reference value, and NaN matches only NaN. The
   largest absolute and relative difference per column is reported, even when the run passes.

The tolerance is the pipeline's own tolerance for the 1x identity (`RTOL` = 1e-9, `ATOL` = 1e-12).
Spark may add the terms of a sum or average in an order that depends on partitioning, which can
change the last bits. The reported differences show how far below the tolerance they stay.

## 8. Drift rules

1. **Session drift.** If A's protocol medians at positions 1 and 6 differ by more than 10% of the
   first, drift is reported and comparisons are marked as affected. Nothing is re-run silently.
   This is the rule of experiments.md 3.4.
2. **Pairs.** The same rule applies to B (positions 2 and 5) and C (3 and 4). The C pair runs back
   to back, so it shows the variation between protocols with little time for drift.
3. **Memory.** Pairs whose median peak total RSS differs by more than 0.2 GiB are reported.
4. **Context.** For each protocol, the start time, the free memory before each run, the load
   average and the time since boot are shown next to the pair differences. No rule applies to them.
5. **Earlier records.** A is compared with the stride experiment's stride-7 protocol (2.5)
   descriptively only, with `wall_s` minus `plan_capture` (5), since the code state and the day
   differ.

Drift does not void the results. It is reported, and section 9 still applies.

## 9. Comparing configurations

For two configurations X and Y:

- d1 is the difference between their protocol medians in positions 1–3;
- d2 is the same difference in positions 4–6;
- d is the difference between the medians of their six measured runs.

Under a drift that changes linearly with position, d1 and d2 shift in opposite directions for every
pair: by one position step for A–B and for B–C, by two for A–C. A drift alone therefore gives d1
and d2 opposite signs, and the rules below never report it as a difference.

The rules:

- **Wall time.** X and Y differ if |d| is more than 10% of A's six-run median and d1, d2 and d have
  the same sign. Otherwise there is no clear difference.
- **Peak memory.** The same rule, with a threshold of 0.2 GiB on the median peak total RSS. That is
  just above the largest spread among the measured runs of one protocol in the stride experiment
  (0.185 GiB), the runs this statistic uses. Counting warm-ups, two protocols spread more (0.246
  and 0.223 GiB).
- **Phases** are described with d1, d2 and d, without a threshold.
- **Plans, partition counts, task counts and file counts** are described, not tested.

With two protocols per configuration, this is a descriptive rule, not a statistical test.

## 10. Acceptance criteria

The results are used only if all of these hold:

1. **Code state:** 3.1 holds in every protocol JSON and every `run.json` of the experiment.
2. **Inputs:** each run's `verified_sha256` holds exactly the seven inputs of 2.2, each equal to the
   hash in the stride-7 `config.json`, and each run's `windows_config` equals that file. After the
   session, the seven hashes are computed once more and are unchanged.
3. **Settings:** section 6, items 1 and 2.1–2.4, hold for every run of the used protocols.
4. **Results:** every run of the used protocols ended `ok` with zero check violations. Section 7
   passes for every run of the used protocols and for the stride-experiment run.
5. **Completeness:** each of the six positions has a used protocol (3.4) that started 4 of 4 runs,
   all of which ended `ok`. None stopped early, none was aborted, and no sample exceeded 4.80 GiB.

If criterion 1, 2 or 3 fails, no configurations are compared until the cause is found. Stops and
re-runs follow 3.3 and 3.4. Drift (section 8) is not an acceptance criterion.

Run conditions are not an acceptance criterion either. A departure from 3.2 is recorded as a
deviation, and the protocol's results are labeled with it, as in experiments.md 5.3.

## 11. Predictions

_The author writes this section before any measured run._ For each configuration it gives:

- the median wall time, with a band;
- the peak memory statistic of section 5, with a range;
- the plans, partition counts and task counts expected.

The abort limits follow from the predicted medians (3.3). The stride experiment's predictions
(experiments.md section 4) stay unchanged.

## 12. Deferred
